# Retro Music Toolkit
### An 8-bit / 16-bit game music workstation built for AI agents
**Fully local, no API. The same score always renders the same audio.**
[](#what-it-does-for-you) [](#what-it-does-for-you) [](#what-it-does-for-you) [](#technical-details)
[](#quick-start) [](LICENSE)
🎧 Listen online · Quick start · vs. music models · Technical details
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What it does for you

**🔒 Fully local — no model, no account**\
No API key, no GPU, no cloud calls, no per-generation bill
ing. Once dependencies are installed it runs with the network unplugged. Your scores and audio never
leave your machine.

**🔁 Reproducible output**\
The same JSON and the same seed render the same audio — today, next year,
on another computer. Drum noise, humanize jitter and random arpeggios are all derived from the seed
, so you can commit a score to Git and manage music the way you manage code.

**✏️ Change one note without starting over**\
Bass wrong in bar 9? `patch` edits that one note, leav
es everything else untouched and returns a per-field change log. You never lose the parts you were h
ing else untouched and returns a per-field change log. You never lose the parts you were happy with.

**🩺 Tells you where it is wrong**\
Non-chord tones on strong beats, bass clashing with the chord, pa
rallel fifths, unresolved leaps, a loop seam that never returns to the opening chord — diagnostics r
eport the bar and the note ID, and often the exact repair value.

> [!TIP]
> Want to hear it first? 👉 **Listen online** (five original game cues: an orchestral cave m
arket, a swing-jazz tavern, a subtractive-synth crystal descent, an NES-style boss battle and an orc

hestral waltz finale; English and Chinese)
> Every example is rendered offline from a JSON score in

this repository. Audio synthesis uses no music generation service.
> The repository ships the five M
P3 previews and editable score JSONs only; WAV masters are rendered locally from the scores.

## How is this different from a music generation model
They solve different problems.
| | Music generation model | Retro Music Toolkit |

| **Input** | A text description | A JSON score |
| **Runs on** | Cloud API / local GPU | An ordinar

y laptop, offline |
| **Cost** | Per generation | Zero |
| **Reproducibility** | Same prompt, differ

ent result | Same score, same result |
| **Editing** | Regenerate the whole piece | Change a single

note |
| **Explainability** | You get audio | You get a score and diagnostics |
| **Source material*
* | Training data is not traceable | Procedural sounds plus traceable CC0 / CC BY samples |
**A generation model is good at handing you a first idea. This toolkit is good at turning an idea in
to something that ships in a game, can be revised, and renders the same way every time.** If you alr
eady have a melody in mind, or you are building an AI agent that needs dependable output, this is th
e one you will use every day.
## Who it is for
| ✅ A good fit | ❌ Not a good fit |
| Building a composition or game-dev **AI agent** that needs stable, verifiable tool calls | You wan

t one sentence in and a finished song out |
| **Indie game developers** who need loopable, endlessly

revisable BGM | You need vocals, recorded instruments or modern pop production |
| Environments tha
t must be **offline**, **dependency-free** and **licence-clean** | You need bit-exact chip emulation

(NSF / VGM playback) |
| Treating music like code: version control, review, CI | You never want to
touch structured data |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **It does not compose for you.** You (or your agent) supply the melody; it validate
s, constrains, renders and reports. `hardware` mode is an audible approximation, not bit-accurate 2A
03 / YM2612 / BRR emulation. The examples are verified at the signal level only, with no subjective
listening review — whether they sound good is for you to judge.
## Capabilities

**✍️ Compose**
- Cross-bar sustain (`hold`) and clip cropping
- Motif development: sequence, inversi

on, retrograde, augmentation, ornaments
- Harmony-driven: `harmonize` for accompaniment, `arpeggiate

` for arpeggios
- Swing and humanize, derived from the seed

**🩺 Diagnose**
- Harmony: non-chord tones, bass clashes, parallel fifths/octaves, out-of-key notes
-

Loops: does the last phrase really return to the first?
- Arrangement: melodic breathing, register

crowding, hi-hat density, section contrast
- `describe` text structure, `roll` / `report` piano roll

**🔊 Sound**
- NES-, Genesis- and SNES-inspired profiles, 15 synthesized presets (incl. 4 subtractive

Single-voice chord arpeggio: a triad costs one voice
- SNES eight-tap FIR echo, 8 drum pieces plus s

e chord arpeggio: a triad costs one voice
- SNES eight-tap FIR echo, 8 drum pieces plus sampled kits

**📦 Deliver**
- 44.1 / 48 kHz PCM16 WAV, loop and one-shot
- True peak (4x oversampled) and BS.1770-

4 loudness
- Optional dither, peak limiter and loop crossfade
- `compare` for level-matched A/B expo

loudness
- Optional dither, peak limiter and loop crossfade
- `compare` for level-matched A/B export
### Designed for AI agents
- **JSON in, JSON out**: every command returns structured data; errors carry a machine-readable `cod

e`
- **Meaningful exit codes**: `0` success, `1` tool error, `2` invalid score
- **Token-aware**: st

din / stdout, `--compact`, `--bars 9-16` to work on a section
- **Self-verifying**: validation error
s include the repair value; `patch` returns a per-field diff
